state.issue:
perf(yq): cursor_key's sibling scan makes per-item key/path reads O(fields) each, quadratic over a wide mapping

## Symptom

Any query that asks `key` (or `path`, or `parent`) once per member of a wide
mapping is quadratic in the number of members. Release build, M5 Max, flat
mappings of `kN: N`:

| query | 20k keys | 40k keys | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[.[] \| key \| path] \| length` | 64.2 s | 275.9 s | 4.3x for 2x input |
| `[.[] \| select(key == "k5")] \| length` | 31.0 s | 125.8 s | 4.1x for 2x input |
| `[.[] \| key \| line] \| length` | 0.02 s | 0.03 s | linear (the walk route) |

A ratio of ~4 for a doubling is the signature of O(n^2). The third row is the
same document and the same `key`, answered by the path-context *walk*, and it
is linear — so this is not `key` being expensive, it is one route being
quadratic.

## Cause

`cursor_slot` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`, `cursor_key`'s worker before #2763
renamed it) answers "where does this cursor sit in its parent" by walking the
parent's members until one matches by `same_node`:

```rust
let mut f = fields.clone();
while let Some((field, rest)) = f.uncons() {
    if field.value_cursor.same_node(c) || field.key_cursor.same_node(c) { ... }
    f = rest;
}
```

That is O(fields) per call, and `cursor_path_and_ancestors` calls it once per
level of the climb. Any route that asks it per item — `eval_builtin`'s cursor
arm and the owned-identity pipe both do — pays O(n) per item over an n-member
mapping. The walk route avoids it entirely by carrying the trail, which is why
the third row above is linear.

This predates #2763 and is unchanged by it: the same table on the merge-base
binary gives the same numbers. #2763 only makes the scan's existence easier to
see, because it added a second `same_node` test to the same loop.

## Likely shape of a fix

The member's position is derivable in O(1) from the tree rather than by
scanning: #2763 added `DocumentCursor::prev_sibling` and both indexed formats
lay a member out as consecutive key/value siblings. What is missing is the
*index* — "which member is this" — which `path`/`key`-on-an-array needs. A rank
over the parent's child positions would answer both in O(1)/O(log n) without a
scan, and the BP structure already carries the machinery.

Worth measuring first whether the array arm (`uncons_cursor` counting up to an
index) or the object arm dominates in practice; the table above is object-only.

## Verification notes

- Gate on output identity, and re-run the three rows above at 20k/40k/80k: the
  fix should turn 4.3x-for-2x into ~2x-for-2x, which is the claim.
- `[.[] | key | line]` (the walk route) must stay exactly where it is — it does
  not touch this scan today and a "fix" that routes it through one would be a
  regression.
- Both architectures: the pinned boxes disagree by more than noise on
  memory-bound effects (see CLAUDE.md's benchmarking discipline).
